rules.statement: Don't report reading `IOptions<T>.Value` in a constructor as a defect when sibling services in the same package read options the same way: `IOptions<T>` is bound once at start-up, so the value doesn't go stale, and `IOptionsMonitor<T>` is the type for values that change while running.
rules.why: The maintainer declined this finding: `IOptions<T>` gives the same value on every request, and the configuration conventions use `IOptionsMonitor<T>` only for values that change at runtime.
rules.check: Before flagging a constructor that reads `.Value`, check whether the type is `IOptions<T>` rather than `IOptionsMonitor<T>`, and whether sibling handlers or services in the package already read `.Value` in their constructors. If both hold, don't report it.

rules.statement: Build a protocol well-known path, such as `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, from the shared constant that already defines it, not from a string literal.
rules.why: A second copy of the path can drift from the path discovery actually serves, and links built from it would then point to the wrong address.
rules.check: Look for string literals of well-known or endpoint paths in new code when a shared constant for the same path already exists.

rules.statement: When code builds a link to a route, take both the route mapping and the link from one constant, and add a test that the page answers at that path.
rules.why: If the link's constant isn't the source of the mapped route, a route change or library upgrade makes the link return 404 and nothing fails.
rules.check: Look for a new path constant used to build links while the endpoint mapping relies on a library default or a separate literal, with no test that requests the constant's path.

rules.statement: Keep a URL path join, and the path it uses, in one exported helper, and call that helper everywhere instead of repeating the join.
rules.why: Two copies can drift, so the URL shown to the user can differ from the URL actually fetched.
rules.check: Look for the same path literal or `new URL(path, base)` join repeated across modules when a helper or constant already exists for it.

rules.statement: Reuse an exported type for a shape, not an inline copy of it in props or test helpers.
rules.why: Copies of one shape have to change together, and they drift apart when they don't.
rules.check: Look for inline object types whose members match a type that is already exported, in components or in tests.

rules.statement: When new wiring passes data between pieces that are each unit-tested, add at least one test at the composing level that shows the data arrives.
rules.why: Without it, the composing code can drop the data or pass the wrong object, and no test fails.
rules.check: Look for new data flow through a parent or composing component, such as parsed input passed into a child step, where every parent-level test mocks the input without that data.
